articles.title: Cubs BCB After Dark: How does Alex Bregman look now?
articles.summary: The late-night/early-morning spot for Cubs fans asks your thoughts about the big move of last off-season now.
articles.body:
Welcome back to BCB After Dark: the coolest club for night owls, early risers, new parents and Cubs fans abroad. Come on in and join us. It's always good to see a friendly face. There's no cover charge. The dress code is casual. The hostess will seat you now. Bring your own beverage.

BCB After Dark is the place for you to talk baseball, music, movies, or anything else you need to get off your chest, as long as it is within the rules of the site. The late-nighters are encouraged to get the party started, but everyone else is invited to join in as you wake up the next morning and into the afternoon.

Last week I asked you if reliever Daniel Palencia should get sent down to Iowa. You folks were rough as 79 percent of you wanted to see Palencia go down to Des Moines.

Here's the part with the music and the movies. You can do with it what you will. We hope you enjoy it, however.

Sometimes you just got to play the hits. Here's guitarist George Benson, joined by guitarist Carlos Santana, jammin' Benson's hit "Breezin'" on the Midnight Special sometimes in the seventies. I believe this is 1978.

I'm running a bit behind tonight, so I just have a few words to say about Written on the Wind , the 1956 Douglas Sirk-directed melodrama starring Rock Hudson, Lauren Bacall, Robert Stack and Dorothy Malone, who won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her performance.

Douglas Sirk melodramas aren't really my thing, although I do appreciate some things about them. When I do watch them, it's almost always because of the lush Technicolor that pops off the screen. I get so tired of the kind of washed-out dark look that most films today have. The colors are all muddied and the brightness is turned down, even in scenes set outdoors. I've read several explanations for why films today look like that and my response to all of them is "Yes, but you could just not do that." But that would cost more money, I suppose.

Sirk's films are all bright with bold colors that pop. Written on the Wind is maybe the best-looking of Sirk's films. Do the colors look "natural"? Not really, but there's nothing about this soapy melodrama that is natural anyways. If I'm going to watch a film like this, I want to be taken for a ride in a dream. The look of Written on the Wind , as well as the music by Frank Skinner, does that.

The plot of Written on the Wind would be at home in any soap opera of the time. Stack plays Kyle, an insecure and alcoholic son of a rich Texas oil baron. His best friend since childhood is Mitch (Hudson), who is definitely not rich but is always willing to help out Kyle when he needs it.

In a rare period of sobriety, Kyle and Mitch take a trip to New York where they meet Lucy (Bacall), a secretary. Lucy is immediately attracted to Mitch, but it is Kyle who decides to woo her and Mitch, out of deference to his friend, steps away. Eventually Kyle's efforts win Lucy over and the two of them are married.

Meanwhile, Kyle has a sister Marylee (Malone), who is, and these are the films words not mine, a "tramp." We quickly find out that Marylee's wild party-girl persona is because she's been in love with Mitch since childhood and Mitch has no interest in her. Both Kyle and Marylee are spoiled rich kids who are full of anxiety and neuroses.

Eventually, Kyle realizes that his wife Lucy and Mitch are in love and his insecure and jealous nature takes over. On top of that, Marylee schemes and plots to hurt Mitch in the same way his lack of interest her has hurt her. If Lucy gets caught in the blast radius, all the better.

Stack, Hudson and Bacall are all fine actors who do a good job, but the star of this film is Malone and she has the Oscar to prove it. Her part is really about as big as Bacall's and that probably helped her in the Supporting Actress category. But she's also delightfully evil with emotions that go from 0 to 60 in 10 seconds in the way that you want from this kind of movie. If there's a reason to watch Written on the Wind other than how beautiful the colors look, it's Malone as Marylee. Stack also becomes a bit unhinged after he starts drinking again, which is nice, but he can't compare to his character's sister.

These Douglas Sirk melodramas were really just TV soap operas that have the plot tightened up, the production values taken to 11 and populated with actors who can really act. If that sounds like something that interests you, you couldn't do much better than Written on the Wind.

Here's the trailer for Written on the Wind . First, there are two great soap opera slaps in this one for those who are fans of that. Also, even in this short teaser, it's easy to see how Malone's character pops off the screen compared to the others.

Welcome back to everyone who skips the music and movies.

The Cubs big acquisition this past winter was the five-year, $175 million deal with third baseman Alex Bregman. The attitude around here towards that deal was mixed, as it locked up Bregman to the Cubs through his age 36 season at $35 million a year. (Yes, a small percentage of that money is deferred.) I don't think anyone around here complained about the Cubs spending money, but I think there was some complaining that the money could have been spent better elsewhere. Some thought the Cubs should have spent that money bringing back Kyle Tucker, or maybe Kyle Schwarber or Cody Bellinger.

The critics of the move gain some traction as Bregman struggled earlier in the year. Yes, his defense was great and the Cubs infield defense of Bregman, Dansby Swanson, Nico Hoerner and Michael Busch was second-to-none in the first half (and all season when Swanson was healthy). But going into the All-Star break, Bregman was hitting .241/.336/.359. That's not bad, but it's not what you pay $35 million a year for. In particular, Bregman struggled in June and it looked like he was getting worse as the season went on.

He did not get worse. In fact, since the All-Star Break, Bregman has hit .302/.378/.604 and has continued to provide strong defense. Had Bregman done that all season long, his contract would be considered a bargain.

But there is a little more than 4 years left on Bregman's deal. There's no guarantee that his second half will be the new normal going forward. After having seeing Bregman for almost 90 percent of a season, what grade would you give the Bregman contract now?

Thanks for stopping by tonight. We've enjoyed hosting you. Please get home safely. Call a ride if you need to. Recycle any cans and bottles. Don't forget any personal items. Tip your waitstaff. And join us again tomorrow evening for more BCB After Dark.

articles.title: Craig Carton Reveals Why He Joined Outkick for His Next Venture Beyond WFAN
articles.summary: "If you view my show as a startup for OutKick, we’re already ahead of the game. We already have followers that believe in the content. Now, we just have to f...
articles.body:
It's been a busy last twelve months for Craig Carton . Following the cancellation of his FS1 program, Breakfast Ball , in July, many speculated about where Carton's path would lead after his network television debut. The results of that journey to today shouldn't be surprising.

First, Carton remained a partner with FOX and worked with Red Seat Ventures to develop a one-hour daily program titled The Craig Carton Show . His return to WFAN followed, with the official announcement coming in early December. Earlier this year, Carton added another layer to his growing media presence by teaming with Lil Wayne for The Joint Venture podcast. Beginning today, Carton elevates that initial project by bringing The Craig Carton Show to a rebranded and growing OutKick digital platform.

"I have been a frequent guest on OutKick as well as FOX News. So, there's some familiarity that I have with them, and they have with me," said Carton about the early discussions surrounding bringing The Craig Carton Show to OutKick. "I was a guest with Dan [Dakich] about six months ago. Afterwards, they reached out and inquired about my deal with FOX expiring. The interest was mutual."

With Carton's FOX contract coming to an end earlier this summer, the network made an offer to keep him in tow along with The Craig Carton Show podcast. However, the network allowed Carton to retain the podcast and shop it around to other distributors outside of his prior arrangement with SportsGrid .

"I had the ability to go look for other partners, but they [OutKick] had an interest in me. It sort of came together at the same time. I have great respect for FOX as a company. They've been great to me on the sports side. Then to take that and evolve our relationship under the FOX News umbrella was a no-brainer," explained Carton, who co-owns the IP for The Craig Carton Show with FOX. "We're partners in every sense of the word."

The program will be somewhat similar to its initial version, but also very different. It's been more than two months since Carton hosted an episode, but the summer break allowed him to prepare for how he envisions this version reaching an audience that may not be as familiar with him as others.

His approach to discussing the hottest sports topics of the day will not change. The content will be more nationally focused, and less based in New York City sports which brought him success for almost two decades at WFAN. However, the biggest change to the new version of the show lies in something he didn't have an opportunity to do with SportsGrid .

"The biggest change is this show affords me the opportunity to do far more long-form interviews than I've ever really done," said Carton. "I've always felt I'm really good at it, and I love doing it. The last version of the show, because of commercial breaks, didn't allow for real long-form interviews. This version does. Every show, I expect there will be some sort of long-form interview."

What drew Carton to OutKick was the ability to tackle issues he wouldn't discuss in other forums. From pop culture to politics, everything Carton plans to present on the show will be something that interests him, with guest appearances mixed in as well.

Another change at OutKick is that The Craig Carton Show will be a solo act. Former 97.5 The Fanatic host Tyrone Johnson served as Carton's co-host for the past 10 months while the program was on SportsGrid.

"This will be a solo act. Tyrone may make a guest appearance from time to time. I'm very fond of him, and I believe he is a future star in this industry," said Carton.

From a production standpoint, The Craig Carton Show will move from a live, one-hour program to a taped show. Episodes will be released weekdays at 6 p.m. on OutKick's social platforms and YouTube channel . The show will also be posted to The Craig Carton Show YouTube page , which currently has nearly 74,000 subscribers. In the initial announcement , it was stated that the program would be released three days a week on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

"I'd be shocked if, in the first four or five months, we're not doing the show every day," explained Carton. "I don't think we're going to start doing it just three days a week. The best bet for us is to come out of the gate with content five days a week. Building an audience with that kind of quality and consistency."

Carton will host the program from the OutKick offices at the FOX News complex on Sixth Avenue in New York City. Construction continues on Carton's permanent studio, which should open in less than a month. In the meantime, Carton will tape his first OutKick episodes in a smaller setup, then expand the space soon.

The arrangement with OutKick comes after Carton signed a multi-year contract with Audacy's WFAN late last year. Carton explained that there are never any secrets when it comes to business dealings between companies. His aim is full transparency. By allowing every outlet he serves to better understand what's expected while giving him the freedom to expand his opportunities elsewhere.

"WFAN is well aware, and was aware from day one, that OutKick approached me. OutKick is also very aware of my responsibilities to WFAN. Everyone is also very aware that I'm doing the podcast with Lil Wayne. No surprises. We were able to work it out where everyone is happy about the amount of time I'm committing to each entity," explained Carton. "The three actually complement each other really well."

In balancing all of his duties, Carton admits he's not a big sleeper. With The Craig Carton Show becoming a daily program alongside his WFAN responsibilities, his day will begin with the OutKick program before shifting to WFAN just after noon. He says there will likely be some stories that occasionally intertwine from one show to the other. But understanding the belief each company has in him, every outlet will get his full attention.

Carton is a competitor. His motivation has been to be the best at everything he's doing while earning the consumer's time in the process. With the shift to OutKick, that motivation is no different. He stands by his resume of success. His ability to draw younger audiences. In addition, he believes his content model fits what Clay Travis and OutKick have built since its inception.

"OutKick is a well-established platform with brand awareness and name recognition. We're not starting with zero followers on social platforms. We have a built-in audience already there waiting for new content," said Carton. "If you view my show as a startup for OutKick, we're already ahead of the game. We already have followers that believe in the content. Now, we just have to find some new ones. I fully expect a great launch and quick success."

The journey of Craig Carton includes many highs, but also many lows. Many of the low points Carton experienced would easily end a career for others. But now, walking into a partnership with OutKick following a third and successful return to WFAN, Carton says he doesn't take anything for granted anymore.

"There is a different level of satisfaction with this latest return to WFAN," explained Carton. "Coming back from the national show on FS1 and the Red Seat Ventures project. Then having the same level of success again with another new partner. It's hard to explain because my ego isn't there anymore. But the satisfaction I get from enjoying the moments of success now is heightened. Because I know how hard it is to have success in this industry. The success this time around, and what I will have with OutKick, I'm enjoying it more than I ever have."

Carton says the current lineup at WFAN is healthier and more together than at any time previously. He's thrilled to see the wave of success his return has brought to the radio station, mainly ensuring those who hired him that they made the right decision. Carton says he understands his return did come with a price for others.

"I'm sensitive to how the news came out that I was coming back. Whether people thought I was coming back or not. In a perfect world, a company can tell their on-air people before they go on air that this was happening. Obviously, there wasn't an opportunity to do that, and I'm sensitive to that," said Carton. "It's a cutthroat business. If the powers that be didn't think a new version of Craig Carton would be successful, they wouldn't have made the decision to do it. Now, less than a year in, the results prove their decision was the right one and created a very healthy radio station."

Carton's career has experienced plenty of highs and lows, but his return to WFAN has reinforced his belief that he can still connect with an audience and deliver results. Now, he's hoping OutKick experiences the same payoff.

For Carton, this opportunity is about more than adding another show to his schedule. It's another chance to prove his ability to build an audience extends beyond the New York sports market he has dominated for nearly two decades.

WFAN took a calculated risk when it decided Carton was worth bringing home. Less than a year later, the results have validated that decision and helped create a healthy radio station. Now, OutKick is making its own bet.

Carton believes the upside can be just as significant. He knows success has to be earned, regardless of the platform or his previous accomplishments.

If the bet pays off, OutKick may eventually look back on its decision much the same way WFAN does today — as a chance that became a very good investment.

articles.title: Hernández’s 3-run homer and Sheehan’s 10 Ks power Dodgers past Reds 6-3 for 5th straight win
articles.summary: Teoscar Hernández hit a three-run homer, Emmet Sheehan tied a career high with 10 strikeouts in his first major league outing since Aug. 2 and the Los Angele...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Teoscar Hernández hit a three-run homer, Emmet Sheehan tied a career high with 10 strikeouts in his first major league outing since Aug. 2 and the Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the Cincinnati Reds 6-3 on Monday night.

Shohei Ohtani went 0 for 3 with two strikeouts and a walk in his return to the lineup after a four-day break to heal multiple lingering injuries.

The NL West leaders won their fifth in a row despite being outhit 7-3. For the second time in franchise history, the Dodgers won after scoring six or more runs on just three hits. They cooled off the Reds, who were coming off series wins over the Chicago Cubs, San Diego Padres and NL Central-leading Milwaukee.

It was the first of seven games over the next 11 days between the teams.

Sheehan (5-8) allowed one run and three hits in 5 2/3 innings. He was recalled earlier in the day from Triple-A Oklahoma City, where he'd been sent due to his struggles on the mound.

Evan Phillips pitched a 1-2-3 ninth to earn his first save since May 2, 2025.

The Dodgers didn't get their first hit until Hernández singled off reliever Brandon Williamson (3-4) leading off the fifth. Alex Call was hit by a pitch with two outs, and both runners scored on a throwing error by third baseman Ke'Bryan Hayes.

Trailing 2-1, the Reds loaded the bases against Sheehan in the sixth after Carlos Jorge singled for his first major league hit. Alex Vesia entered and threw a called third strike past JJ Bleday to end the threat.

Hernández homered off Williamson in the bottom half to make it 5-1.

The Reds' first two runs came on homers to center field by De La Cruz in the first and Eugenio Suárez in the seventh.

De La Cruz has gone deep in three straight games. He has 24 homers this season, one short of equaling his own club record for switch-hitters set in 2024.

Cincinnati closed to 5-3 in the eighth on pinch-hitter Dane Myers' RBI groundout against reliever Jack Dreyer.

Pinch-hitter Will Smith tacked on a sacrifice fly for Los Angeles in the bottom half.

Reds starter Chase Burns struck out five in three hitless innings before leaving as part of the team's workload-management plan that went into place Monday.

Reds LHP Nick Lodolo (3-3, 5.08 ERA) starts Tuesday against Dodgers LHP Tarik Skubal (8-7, 2.86).

articles.title: New York Giants Cut Their Longest-Tenured Player Darius Slayton
articles.summary: In a surprise move on Monday, the New York Giants cut wide receiver Darius Slayton. Slayton was the longest-tenured Giant, […]
articles.body:
In a surprise move on Monday, the New York Giants cut wide receiver Darius Slayton.

Slayton was the longest-tenured Giant, having been with the team since they selected him with the 171 st pick in the 2019 NFL Draft. For his career, he appeared in 106 games, caught 296 passes for 4,435 yards with 22 touchdowns.

In 2025, he caught 37 passes for 538 yards with one touchdown. Slayton was one of the most respected players in the locker room. But he's been plagued by drops throughout his career and was at the bottom of the depth chart heading into this season.

General manager Joe Schoen re-signed Slayton to a three-year, $36 million deal last offseason. He was set to make $13 million for the upcoming season.

By releasing the veteran wideout, the Giants will save a little over $3 million, but they will have a dead cap hit of $12.749 million.

It became apparent once John Harbaugh was hired as head coach that he was not high on Slayton. Early in free agency, the team signed Darnell Mooney and Calvin Austin. Then in the draft, the Giants traded up into the third round to select Malachi Fields with the 74 th overall pick.

In June, New York signed veteran receivers Odell Beckham Jr, JuJu Smith-Schuster, and Braxton Berrios. Although Slayton made the initial roster, it was reported that he would be inactive for most game days, as the team plans to use more 12 personnel packages this season with two tight ends and two receivers. These factors ultimately led to the team parting ways with him.

"Grateful for my time in NY. 7 years a Giant nothing but love for one of the most prestigious organizations in the NFL. Excited to see what's next." Slayton said on X following his release.

His 4,435 receiving yards rank 12 th most in the history of the franchise, but now he'll have to write a new chapter with another organization.

articles.title: Swansea's golden boot winner yet to kick start season
articles.summary: Zan Vipotnik has been backed to return to form for Swansea City, even though he is still not guaranteed to return to the starting side.
articles.body:
Zan Vipotnik has been backed to return to form for Swansea City – even though he is still not guaranteed to return to the starting line-up.

Swansea are flying in the Championship, leading the table after six games, and they take their unbeaten start to Southampton on Tuesday (19:45 BST).

And yet their leading goalscorer of last season has not got up and running.

Vipotnik, 24, took the second-tier golden boot with 23 league goals last term for a side that did not trouble the eventual race for the play-offs.

The tally was built on an eye-catching start where he had bagged five goals from the opening six games.

The same number of appearances into the 2026-27 season, and Vipotnik is still to find the net.

The latest chance came in the latter stages of Saturday's goalless Welsh derby with Wrexham, Vipotnik having looked lively off the bench was unable to steer his stretch past Anthony Patterson to break the deadlock.

Swans boss Vitor Matos, though, appears calm.

Asked whether he expected the Slovenia international to find confidence and form soon, he replied: "I think if someone knows how to score goals it's him, so I think it's just a matter of scoring."

The obvious difference is that Vipotnik has only been given one league start so far this year, Adam Idah preferred in every game since the opening day win at Stoke City.

Idah, a £6m signing from Celtic a year ago, missed most of last season with injury, but has looked ready to make his mark with two goals so far.

There have also been the question marks over Vipotnik's future.

There was the school of thought that Swansea might want to cash in on the high value of a player who out-performed his expected goals (xG) by some way last season.

In other words, he scored more goals than the chances suggested he had a right to.

The signing of Ross Stewart following the Scotland international's departure from Southampton only added weight to that theory.

But the only concrete bid was turned down, Hull City's £10m offer knocked back, while Matos claimed he was not aware of deadline day interest from Burnley.

The Portuguese did concede transfer windows still open elsewhere – most notably in Saudi Arabia – still mean a departure cannot be ruled out.

Former Wales striker Nathan Blake, who valued Vipotnik at around £25m, said the speculation and shift to the bench will have hit Vipotnik, claiming late last month: "I could see by looking at his face, he's not on it. He's probably two or three yards short mentally because of what is going on."

Last week Matos conceded it might have had an impact, saying: "It's normal that some things can unsettle you when we are in the middle of all of this."

With Stewart injured for Tuesday's game with his former side, and Swansea likely to rotate for a third match in seven days, Matos was asked whether this was the game to reintroduce Vipotnik to the starting line-up.

"We need to see what is best for the team," said Matos, offering a smile but no commitment.

What he did offer, though, was conviction that the player of last season is still there in more ways than one.

"Besides the goals, he contributes a lot for the other parts of the game," said Matos.

"I think against Wrexham he came on really sharp with the right mindset, fought for the duels, fought for the first ball, second ball, tried to arrive in the box for that chance.

"Even with that he was helping building.

"So all that is coming - then it's just a matter of scoring and he will score for sure."

Swansea would welcome that as they look to show their impressive start should be taken seriously.

Their record of conceding just once so far is the meanest in the EFL, although they take on a Saints team who put five past Millwall last time out at St Mary's.

"Southampton I think is one of the best teams on the league, a proper contender to win the league and to get promoted," said Matos. "So it will be a really good game.

"We need to analyse the Wrexham game, see the priorities and then see as well Southampton.

"But I expect a really, really good game for us to compete."

articles.title: Barry-Murphy urges calm after winless Cardiff start
articles.summary: Brian Barry-Murphy insists Cardiff should not be too downbeat about their unfavourable league position after a winless start to the Championship campaign.
articles.body:
Brian Barry-Murphy insists Cardiff should not be too downbeat about their unfavourable league position after a winless start to the Championship campaign.

The Bluebirds begin the week in the relegation places following a 2-0 defeat to Portsmouth on Saturday which leaves them on three points after five games.

Stoke will arrive at the Cardiff City Stadium for Tuesday evening's game (19:45 BST) buoyed by their 4-0 thrashing of Charlton over the weekend.

But head coach Barry-Murphy has urged supporters and players to remain calm, and reiterated that there is still a long way to go this season.

"It's a tough schedule. We knew these games were very close together in this opening period. With the squad the size of ours, that has its challenges," said the Irishman.

"I wouldn't get too carried away by where we are. As I say, it's still very early in the season. We have to remain calm."

Barry-Murphy - who won promotion from League One in his first season in charge of the Welsh club - added: "We have worked together for a period with a lot of these players. We know how we work, and we've got to improve. That will remain the case.

"We said it all last season; it's a very young team, and we need to help them and show them consistency in how we play. That is the route forward."

Many Cardiff supporters have voiced their displeasure after being left short on squad numbers, with only four players added in the summer transfer window.

Barry-Murphy is no closer, either, to welcoming any of his injured players back to the side, and appears to have lost forward Isaak Davies too.

The 48-year-old coach admitted there is no clear timescale for the return of club captain Calum Chambers, who is yet to feature this season.

"Isaak Davies felt his hamstring in training on Friday. I imagine he won't be available on Tuesday," he explained.

"The rest of the guys are back around the international break, I think, so I don't imagine anything will change between now and Tuesday.

"Calum Chambers is in the same bracket as Dylan [Lawlor] and Will Fish. He won't be available for Tuesday, and his timescale is slightly more complicated because of his injury."

Asked whether he feels Cardiff have enough to go again at short notice, Barry-Murphy said: "We have no choice.

"The players who are here will have our full support to help them try to produce a performance to win.

"We are very confident we can win games at this level, and I'm sure we will. The fans always [give us energy].

"We don't take that for granted. We understand that our job is to produce a performance on Tuesday that gives us a chance to win."

EVANSVILLE, Ind. (WEHT) — The University of Southern Indiana women's volleyball managed to steal one set away in their 3-1 loss against the 21st ranked Indiana Hoosiers Monday afternoon.

Screaming Eagles head coach Jeffrey Aucoin said he hopes his team can build upon the winning set and take it with them through the rest of the season.

"We were a little bit more aggressive," he said. "You know we were just missing in the first set I think set two things started to go our way. We're we're getting back into our rhythm and we're just trying to build momentum. It's easy in these types of matches to put pressure on being perfect and dominating and want to prove everybody something, but, it's really important that you just put pressure on creating opportunities. And I think that's what we did in that second set and we took advantage of those opportunities to finish out the set."

Next, Southern Indiana will head to Columbus, Ohio to compete in the Sports Import Classic starting with Youngstown State on Friday, September 11th.

articles.title: Ajay Mitchell predicted to become one of the breakout players of the 2026-27 NBA season
articles.summary: After a superb sophomore season, Ajay Mitchell is destined for great things with the Thunder.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder have made some major changes ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season. Of course, the core players are still there, but it does mean that Ajay Mitchell is set for a bigger role. He will play a massive role in the backcourt alongside Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

It is yet to be decided whether he will be the starter alongside SGA, as he will be competing against Cason Wallace for that role. Even if he plays off the bench, Mitchell will be a big part of the Thunder 's potential success in the 2026-27 season.

Ajay Mitchell is projected to be a breakout star in the 2026-27 season

With rotation players like Aaron Wiggins, Isaiah Joe, and Lu Dort all leaving the Thunder, the team needs a boost from the remaining players. Mitchell must play a big role because they need his contributions on both sides of the floor.

He is a decent defender who can fill the Dort void, but he will be mainly relied upon for his offensive contributions. Mitchell is a natural scorer who can create his own opportunities, but he can also set his teammates up with good passes.

Wallace will probably be the resident defensive stopper now, so the starting guard role alongside SGA is still up in the air. However, Mitchell is still set for a big year because no matter what, the Thunder will need him to step up and live up to the hype.

"Over the last two seasons, Mitchell has played only 93 games because of the Thunder's depth. That depth has gotten a little thinner with OKC moving off Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins, and Isaiah Joe. And all of that means more minutes and opportunities for Mitchell," Bleacher Report's Mo Dakhil said in an article about players ready to take the leap .

As long as Mitchell can keep making an impact, the future is bright for the Thunder. They already have a monumental core group, but having Mitchell break out will only be a boost to their chances of winning the championship again after missing out in the 2026 Playoffs.

Fans only need to wait 6 more days until the Steel City brand of football returns when the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Atlanta Falcons on September 13. In the spirit of the countdown to kickoff, we'll take a look at the most recent and best players ever to wear No. 6.

Steelers current No. 6: LB Patrick Queen

Queen, who signed with the Steelers as a free agent in 2024, is the current No. 6 wearer on the team's roster.

Steelers training camp: Early photos of action in Latrobe

Best No. 6 in Steelers history: QB Bubby Brister

No. 6 doesn't have the historical impact as other numbers on our countdown to kickoff, but the greatest wearer is without a doubt quarterback Bubby Brister.

Brister, selected by Pittsburgh with the 67th overall pick in the third round of the 1986 NFL Draft, spent seven years with the Steelers (1986-1992) and recorded 10,104 passing yards and 51 touchdowns.

He eventually passed the torch to quarterback Neil O'Donnell following the arrival of head coach Bill Cowher, but remains the greatest Steeler ever to wear No. 6 in franchise history.
